scope: Theorem 6.1 (Absolute stability at a fixed displacement) of the manuscript “Signed cylinder propagation and marked polygons on the honeycomb lattice” (preprints/Signed-cylinder-propagation-and-marked-polygons-on-the-honeycomb-lattice-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2dda2109318f92bb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is 0 < d0 < 1/2 with the following property. Fix a compact set Θ ⊂ C, and fix either a pre-collision displacement −d0 < d < 0 or a post-collision displacement 0 < d < d0. There are constants c > 0 and C < ∞, depending on d and Θ, such that the following holds for every positive integer T and θ ∈ Θ. Consider a finite configuration Y with distinct real positions on R/TZ, using the six basic labels in the pre-collision case and those labels together with Fpair in the post-collision case. Give it a state path p with jumps −qi and closure in Z2/8Z(1, −1). Let nj be the number of physical particles in [j, j + 1), and let pc,j = p1(j+) + p2(j+) √ 2 , 0 ≤ j < T. Then |Wd,θ(Y, p)| ≤ exp  CT − c T−1 X j=0 (n2 j + p2 c,j)   in the post-collision case. The same bound holds for Wpre d,ℜθ(Y, p) in the pre-collision case.
